subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How do you say “I find horror films scary”?
options: La película de terror me dan miedo
Las películas de terror me dan miedo
Las películas de terror me dan igual
Las películas de terror me dan risa
questions.explain: “Dar miedo” = “to frighten”, so “me dan miedo” = “they scare me”.
“Montar a caballo” means “to go horse riding”.
'El ocio' means 'leisure / free time'; it is a false friend with English 'office' (which is 'la oficina').

questions.q: How do you say “You should drink plenty of water”?
questions.explain: “Se debe” = “one should” and “beber” (not “comer”) is used for drinks: “Se debe beber mucha agua”.
“Engordar” means “to put on weight / get fat”; the opposite is “adelgazar”.
'El bienestar' literally means 'being well' and translates as 'wellbeing'.
“Estar en forma” means “to be fit / in good shape”.

questions.q: How would you write 'limpio' to describe two beaches ('playas')?
questions.explain: 'Playa' is feminine, so the plural adjective is feminine plural: 'limpias'.
“La fiebre” means “fever/temperature”, so “tengo fiebre” = “I have a fever”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I'm keen on cooking”?
questions.explain: “Me apasiona” + infinitive = “I'm passionate/keen on”; “cocinar” = to cook (not “coser” = to sew).

questions.q: Which sentence means “Junk food is bad for your health”?
options: La comida sana es mala para la salud
La comida basura es buena para la salud
La comida basura está mala para la salud
La comida basura es mala para la salud
questions.explain: “La comida basura” = junk food and “mala para la salud” = bad for your health.
“Quedarse” = to stay, so “quedarse en casa” = “to stay at home”.

questions.q: How do you say “I have a headache”?
questions.explain: “Me duele la cabeza” = “my head hurts / I have a headache”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I'm a fan of pop music”?
options: Soy aficionada a la música clásica
Soy aficionado a la música pop
Estoy aficionado a la música pop
questions.explain: “Ser aficionado a” = “to be a fan of”, so “Soy aficionado a la música pop”.
“La muela” means a “molar/back tooth”, so “me duele la muela” = toothache.
“Salir de marcha” is a colloquial phrase meaning “to go out / go partying”.
“Estar resfriado” means “to have a cold”.

questions.q: How do you say 'I prefer reading to watching TV'?
options: Prefiero leyendo a ver la televisión
Prefieres leer a ver la televisión
Prefiero ver la televisión a leer
Prefiero leer a ver la televisión
questions.explain: 'Preferir A a B' uses infinitives: 'Prefiero leer a ver la televisión' = 'I prefer reading to watching TV'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'You must avoid sugary drinks'?
options: Hay que evitar las bebidas azucaradas
questions.explain: 'Hay que' = 'one must' and 'evitar' = 'to avoid', so 'Hay que evitar las bebidas azucaradas' = 'You must avoid sugary drinks'.
“Me parece aburrido” = “I find it boring” (agreeing with masculine “el golf”).
“Equilibrada” = balanced, so “una dieta equilibrada” = “a balanced diet”.

questions.q: Which means 'I used to play football every weekend' (habitual past)?
options: Jugué al fútbol todos los fines de semana
Jugaba al fútbol todos los fines de semana
Juego al fútbol todos los fines de semana
Jugaré al fútbol todos los fines de semana
questions.explain: Habitual past actions use the imperfect: 'jugaba' = 'I used to play'.
